messages:
Nina (PM): Quick design sync: we need to finalize the Spend panel layout before dev handoff. Main questions: default scope (Org vs Project), where to surface "Export PDF/CSV", and how to show token breakdown without overwhelming users. Thoughts? Theo D.: My vote: Org-first default, with a prominent scope pill at top-left so users can switch quickly. Project view should be persistent per user (remember last choice). Priya S.: On token breakdown—instead of a single complex stacked area, try a two-row approach: top row = total spend sparkline, bottom row = token breakdown as segmented bars by model. Easier to scan. Elliot R.: I like segmented bars. Also propose a mini-legend that collapses into an accessible toggle to reduce clutter. For mobile, collapse the token models into a popover. Nina (PM): Good. Copy: what do we call the download action? Current label "Download invoice" confuses people who want CSV exports. Options: "Download statement (PDF)", "Export CSV", separate buttons. Priya S.: Separate actions is clearer: show primary CTA = "Download statement (PDF)" in header, and a secondary "Export CSV" near the token table. For per-project rows, put a kebab menu ⋯ with "Export project statement" and "Export project CSV" entries. Theo D.: UX nit: avoid too many CTAs in the header. Could be primary + ellipsis menu in header to hide CSV. That keeps the visual weight low. A11yBot: Reminder: ensure all chart interactions are keyboard accessible. Provide aria-labels for all legends, and a descriptive aria-describedby for the main chart region. When switching scope, announce via aria-live: "Scope changed to Project". Elliot R.: Minimal example for aria-live (to include in spec): ```html
``` Priya S.: Also ensure CSV columns have stable headers: date, org_id, project_id, model, tokens_input, tokens_output, cost_usd. Screen readers rely on those labels. Nina (PM): Good point. Any opinions on timeline granularity control? Daily/Weekly/Monthly? Theo D.: Default to Monthly for billing, let power users switch to Weekly. Hide Daily behind an "advanced" toggle. A11yBot: Chart contrast: avoid low-contrast pastel segments. Aim for WCAG AA contrast for text and AA for graphical objects when possible. Use colorblind-safe palette (Okabe-Ito or similar). Elliot R.: UX flow question: Should the Project list be inline (left rail) or an overlay panel when you click into org? Overlay feels less context-switchy. Inline rail is faster for power users. Priya S.: Overlay is nicer for small orgs, but for orgs with many projects the rail supports quick scanning. Maybe default overlay but allow pinning the rail. Nina (PM): That works. On invoices: backend currently generates monthly PDFs per org only. BillingOps, can we get per-project PDF generation? BillingOps: We can add per-project PDF job. Estimate 10 days to add job + queueing and S3 links. We can expose a temp URL for downloads in the meantime. Nina (PM): Great. Last item: accessibility tests before launch — keyboard nav, screen-reader walkthrough, and contrast audit. Who owns? A11yBot: I'll create a checklist and a sample NVDA VoiceOver script. Theo D.: I'll produce two layout mockups (overlay vs pinned rail) and a small interaction prototype. Priya S.: I'll finalize copy strings and help modal text explaining "tokens", "model share", and "billing period". Elliot R.: I'll write dev notes for lazy-loading mini charts and an intersection observer fallback. Nina (PM): Thanks everyone — please upload your assets to the Figma/Confluence page and tag this thread when ready. Target handoff by end of week. :rocket:
